critical_code_review_comments: routes/haiku.py — EMERGENT_LLM_KEY is read at module-import time via os.environ[...]. If the key is missing at startup the whole router (and thus the app) refuses to import and the backend fails to boot. Prefer os.environ.get with a startup-time check inside the handler so a missing key returns a clear 500 rather than preventing server start.

routes/paging.py pager_event — relies on routes.device_auth.verify_device_token for optional HMAC. If DEVICE_AUTH_REQUIRED=false (seed default), ANY unauthenticated caller on the public internet can POST to /api/paging/event and spoof a page carrying arbitrary resident context (cap_code→resident enrichment happens server-side). Before going live at a facility, either enforce HMAC on /paging/event or gate by network VLAN.

routes/medications.py /due/by-room/{room} and /ack/{reminder_id} are fully public. Anyone reaching the backend URL can enumerate reminders for any room and silently ack them, causing residents to miss medications. Same HMAC/VLAN caveat as paging; worth at minimum validating a kiosk-token on these two endpoints.

routes/medications.py due_for_room — time match is exact HH:MM equality against server UTC. A kiosk that polls every 60s can miss a reminder if the poll cycle drifts or the server restarts during the minute window. Consider a ±1-minute window (already mentioned in the docstring but not implemented), or store a last-fired_at stamp per reminder and compare `now >= scheduled_today AND last_fired < scheduled_today`.
routes/medications.py time_hhmm has no regex/format validation on input — a caller can POST '25:99' and it will simply never fire. Add a Pydantic validator: `re.fullmatch(r'[0-2]\d:[0-5]\d', v)`.

routes/haiku.py — generate_today loops residents sequentially with one Claude roundtrip each. For 6 residents it takes ~20-30s (admin waits blocking). Consider asyncio.gather with a small semaphore (e.g., 3) to parallelise while staying under rate limits.

routes/haiku.py — stores haikus unbounded; no pruning. After N months the haikus collection grows linearly. Add a TTL index on created_at (e.g., 90 days) since /latest only needs the newest per resident.

routes/paging.py /event — no rate limiting. A buggy bridge repeatedly posting the same cap_code would flood /feed and hide real pages behind 50-item limit. Consider dedup within 30s window on (cap_code, message).
FloorPlanTab — polling interval not visible in review_request but docstring says 5s; confirm the component clears the interval on unmount to prevent leaks when admin switches tabs.

context_for_next_testing_agent: To re-run iter-6 tests: `REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL=https://elderly-care-voice.preview.emergentagent.com pytest /app/backend/tests/iter6_test.py -v`. Note the login endpoint returns the JWT under the key `token` (NOT `access_token`) — this bit the first draft of the test. Haiku generation takes ~15-25s on first run (6 residents × Claude sync call) so the pytest timeout for /generate-today is set to 180s. Second call is instant (idempotent). The /medications/due/by-room test is inherently time-bound — it creates a reminder at the current UTC HH:MM and for the current weekday; if the UTC minute rolls over between the POST and the GET the test could race — we haven't seen this but it's a known 1-in-60 flake risk. Consider freezing time via a test-only endpoint if this ever flakes.
